definition: knowing everything

examples.text: The novel's omniscient narrator reports the thoughts of every character.
Advisers flattered the king as if he were omniscient.
My mother seems omniscient about which of us ate the last cookie.

confused.note: Omniscient means all-knowing; omnipotent means all-powerful.

questions.passage: The story is told by an ______ narrator. Readers learn not only what each of the four sisters says and does but also what each privately thinks, fears, and hopes.
questions.explanation: A narrator who reports every character's private thoughts knows everything.

distractors.why: Obtrusive means unpleasantly noticeable, which is not what the examples show.
Autonomous means self-governing, which does not describe a narrator's knowledge.
Decisive means settling an issue quickly, which does not fit.

definition: the belief that pleasure is the most important thing in life; living for pleasure

examples.text: Moralists blamed the empire's decline on the hedonism of its rulers.
The poem celebrates the hedonism of a summer with no plans and no clocks.
A week at the beach with no homework was pure hedonism.

confused.note: Hedonism is devotion to pleasure; heroism is great courage.

questions.passage: The philosopher rejected ______ as a guide to living. A life spent chasing one pleasure after another, she argued, leaves a person less satisfied than a life devoted to work that matters.
questions.explanation: Chasing pleasure as life's aim is hedonism.

distractors.why: Empathy is sharing another's feelings, which is not what she rejected.
Acuity is sharpness of mind or senses, which does not fit.
A doctrine is a set of beliefs in general; the specific belief in pleasure is hedonism.

definition: noticeable in a way that is unpleasant or unwanted

examples.text: The film's obtrusive music tells viewers what to feel in every scene.
Residents complained about the obtrusive new tower beside the old church.
The waiter was so obtrusive that we could not finish a sentence.

confused.note: Obtrusive means unpleasantly noticeable; abstruse means hard to understand.

questions.passage: Good stage lighting should go unnoticed. In this production it is ______: spotlights swing wildly across the audience, colors change every few seconds, and the actors are often lost in the glare.
questions.explanation: Lighting that distracts from the play is unpleasantly noticeable.

distractors.why: Intrinsic means belonging naturally, which does not fit.
Concise means brief, which does not describe distracting lights.
Comparable means similar, which does not fit.

partsNote: from Latin trudere, "to thrust": thrusting against

definition: extremely angry

examples.text: The captain is livid when he learns that the map has been sold.
The king was livid at the news that his fleet had been burned.
My sister was livid when she found her sweater stretched out of shape.

confused.note: Livid means furious; vivid means bright and clear.

questions.passage: The author was ______ when she saw the published edition. Without consulting her, the editor had cut two chapters, changed the ending, and given the book a title she had specifically rejected.
questions.explanation: Unauthorized cuts and a rejected title would make her extremely angry.

distractors.why: Sufficient means enough, which does not describe a person's reaction.
Decisive means able to decide quickly, which does not fit.
Autonomous means independent, which does not fit.

definition: sharpness of thought, vision, or hearing

examples.text: The eagle's visual acuity lets it spot a rabbit from two miles away.
The old judge has lost none of her mental acuity.
My grandfather's hearing acuity is remarkable when someone whispers about dessert.

confused.note: Acuity is sharpness of the senses or mind; acumen is good practical judgment.

questions.passage: Pilots must pass a test of visual ______. Each candidate is asked to read letters only a few millimeters high from a distance of six meters, first with one eye and then with the other.
questions.explanation: Reading tiny letters at a distance tests sharpness of vision.

distractors.why: Empathy is sharing another's feelings, which an eye test does not measure.
Conviction is firm belief, which does not fit.
Temperament is a person's nature, which does not fit "visual."

definition: to cause an important change or event to begin or to happen faster

examples.text: The enzyme catalyzes the breakdown of starch into sugar.
The arrest of the bishop catalyzed the revolt.
One teacher's praise catalyzed my interest in writing.

confused.note: To catalyze is to set off change; to categorize is to sort into groups.

questions.passage: Resentment of the new tax had been growing for months. The arrest of a popular shopkeeper who refused to pay it ______ that resentment into open protest, and within a day thousands were in the streets.
questions.explanation: The arrest set off the change from resentment to protest.

distractors.why: Eclipsed means overshadowed, which does not fit turning resentment into protest.
Modified means changed slightly, far weaker than sparking a mass protest.
Absolved means freed from blame, which does not fit.

definition: large in amount, size, or importance

examples.text: The drug produced a substantial drop in blood pressure.
The merchant left a substantial fortune to the city's hospital.
I ate a substantial breakfast before the hike.

confused.note: Substantial means large or solid; to substantiate is to prove.

questions.passage: The repair was not a matter of a few loose tiles. It required ______ work: the entire roof was removed, half the beams were replaced, and the job took four months.
questions.explanation: Replacing the roof over four months is a large amount of work.

distractors.why: Sheer means absolute or very steep; it does not mean large in amount here.
Concise means brief, the opposite of extensive work.
Illicit means illegal, which does not fit.

definition: enough for a particular purpose

examples.text: One drop of blood is sufficient for the test.
The garrison had sufficient food for a month but not for a siege.
Two hours of sleep is not sufficient before an exam.

confused.note: Sufficient means enough; efficient means working without waste.

questions.passage: The committee decided that the evidence was not ______ to justify closing the bridge. Two small cracks, it noted, might be a warning, but engineers would need more data before taking so drastic a step.
questions.explanation: The evidence was not enough to justify the action.

distractors.why: Intrinsic means built in, which does not fit "to justify."
Malicious means intending harm, which does not fit.
Livid means furious, which does not fit.

definition: the act of getting something; or something that has been obtained

examples.text: The acquisition of the port gave the kingdom access to the sea.
Sleep plays a role in the acquisition of new skills.
My latest acquisition is a secondhand guitar with one missing string.

confused.note: An acquisition is something gained; an accusation is a charge of wrongdoing.

questions.passage: The museum's most recent ______ is a set of letters written by the painter to her sister. Bought at auction last spring, they will go on display once conservators have finished cleaning them.
questions.explanation: Letters bought at auction are something the museum obtained.

distractors.why: A conviction is a firm belief or a guilty verdict, which does not fit.
A doctrine is a set of beliefs, which does not fit.
An adversary is an opponent, which does not fit.

definition: a strong belief or opinion; or a formal finding of guilt

examples.text: She spoke with such conviction that the assembly reversed its vote.
The hero's conviction that he is right blinds him to the truth.
It is my firm conviction that breakfast food is acceptable at any hour.

confused.note: A conviction is a firm belief or a guilty verdict; a convention is a custom or a large meeting.

questions.passage: The scientist argued for her theory with great ______. Although every senior colleague disagreed, she never wavered, presenting the same evidence at conference after conference for nearly twenty years.
questions.explanation: Never wavering despite disagreement shows strong belief.

distractors.why: Empathy is sharing others' feelings, which is not what her persistence shows.
Acuity is sharpness, which does not describe unwavering belief.
Hedonism is the pursuit of pleasure, which does not fit.

partsNote: from Latin vincere, "to conquer": thoroughly overcome, convinced

definition: similar in size, amount, or quality, so that a comparison is fair

examples.text: The two groups were comparable in age and health.
No other city of the period was comparable in wealth.
The store brand is comparable in taste and half the price.

confused.note: Comparable means similar enough to compare; comparative means measured by comparison.

questions.passage: To learn whether the new teaching method worked, researchers needed two ______ groups of students. They therefore chose classes from the same school, with the same teacher and nearly identical test scores at the start of the year.
questions.explanation: Classes alike in school, teacher, and scores are similar enough for a fair comparison.

distractors.why: Divergent means differing, the opposite of what the researchers needed.
Autonomous means independent, which is not the requirement described.
Recurrent means happening repeatedly, which does not fit.

partsNote: from Latin par, "equal": able to be made equal

definition: complete and not mixed with anything else; or very steep; or very thin

examples.text: The sheer size of the whale is hard to grasp until one swims beside a boat.
The castle stands on a sheer cliff above the sea.
I finished the race on sheer stubbornness.

confused.note: Sheer means complete, steep, or thin; to shear is to cut.

questions.passage: The team had no star players and little experience. It won the tournament through ______ determination, outrunning and outlasting opponents who were, on paper, far more talented.
questions.explanation: "Sheer determination" means determination and nothing else.

distractors.why: Sufficient means enough; the sentence stresses that determination alone did it.
Concise means brief, which does not describe determination.
Intrinsic means built in, which does not fit the idiom.

definition: a belief or set of beliefs taught by a religion, political party, or other group

examples.text: The party's doctrine held that all land belonged to the state.
The doctrine that the heavens never change was overturned by a new star in 1572.
Our coach's doctrine is simple: defense first.

confused.note: A doctrine is a set of beliefs; a doctorate is the highest university degree.

questions.passage: For most of the century, the army's official ______ was that wars were won by cavalry. Officers who argued that machine guns had made horses useless were ignored or dismissed.
questions.explanation: An official belief taught and enforced by an institution is a doctrine.

distractors.why: An acquisition is something gained, which does not fit.
Temperament is a person's nature, which does not fit an army's official position.
An adversary is an opponent, which does not fit.

definition: having the freedom to govern or control itself; independent

examples.text: The province remained autonomous, with its own laws and courts.
The autonomous vehicle steered through traffic without a driver.
My little sister insists on being autonomous and ties her own shoes, slowly.

confused.note: Autonomous means self-governing; anonymous means unnamed.

questions.passage: Each of the university's twelve colleges is largely ______. It admits its own students, hires its own teachers, and manages its own budget without seeking approval from any central office.
questions.explanation: Running its own admissions, hiring, and budget makes a college self-governing.

distractors.why: Comparable means similar, which is not what the details show.
Obtrusive means unpleasantly noticeable, which does not fit.
Treacherous means disloyal or dangerous, which does not fit.

definition: to be the parts that form something; to be considered as something

examples.text: Nitrogen and oxygen constitute most of the air we breathe.
Farmers constituted nine tenths of the population.
Three slices of pizza do not constitute a balanced meal.

confused.note: To constitute is to make up or amount to; to institute is to establish.

questions.passage: According to the latest figures, women ______ more than half of the country's university students. In medicine and law they now outnumber men by nearly two to one.
questions.explanation: Women make up more than half of the students.

distractors.why: Coincide means to happen at the same time or agree, which does not fit.
Depict means to portray, which does not fit.
Modify means to change slightly, which does not fit.

definition: to suffer something difficult patiently; or to continue to exist for a long time

examples.text: The city endured a siege of nine months.
Their friendship endures through war, distance, and a long silence.
I endured two hours of my cousin's vacation slides.

confused.note: To endure is to bear or to last; to endear is to make beloved.

questions.passage: Few buildings from the period survive, but the old stone bridge has ______. Floods have carried away three of its neighbors, yet it stands as it did when the first carts crossed it six hundred years ago.
questions.explanation: Standing for six hundred years despite floods is lasting a long time.

distractors.why: Coincided means happened at the same time, which does not fit.
Regenerated means grew back, but the bridge was never destroyed.
Emitted means gave off, which does not fit.

definition: to make something seem less important by comparison; to block the light of

examples.text: The younger general's victories soon eclipsed those of his teacher.
The moon eclipses the sun for only a few minutes.
My sister's news about her scholarship eclipsed my news about a new haircut.

confused.note: To eclipse is to overshadow; an ellipse is an oval shape.

questions.passage: The painter was famous in her own day. After her death her reputation was ______ by that of her student, whose bolder canvases came to fill the museums while hers were moved to storage.
questions.explanation: Her student's fame overshadowed her own.

distractors.why: Enhanced means improved, but her reputation declined by comparison.
Constituted means made up, which does not fit.
Absolved means cleared of blame, which does not fit.

definition: able to make decisions quickly and firmly; or settling an issue beyond doubt

examples.text: The battle at the river was the decisive moment of the war.
The 1919 eclipse provided decisive evidence for the theory.
A decisive friend is a blessing when it is time to pick a restaurant.

confused.note: Decisive means settling a matter or quick to decide; derisive means mocking.

questions.passage: The score was tied with seconds remaining. Then came the ______ play: a long pass down the left side that led to the only goal of the match.
questions.explanation: The play that produced the only goal settled the outcome.

distractors.why: Recurrent means happening repeatedly, but this play happened once.
Comparable means similar, which does not fit.
Dreary means dull and gloomy, which does not describe the winning play.

definition: to change something slightly, usually to improve it

examples.text: Engineers modified the wing to reduce drag.
Parliament modified the law after a year of protests.
I modified the recipe by doubling the garlic.

confused.note: To modify is to change slightly; to mollify is to calm someone's anger.

questions.passage: The architects did not abandon their original plan. They ______ it, lowering the roof by two meters and moving the entrance to the south side to satisfy the neighbors' objections.
questions.explanation: Small changes that leave the plan intact are modifications.

distractors.why: Eclipsed means overshadowed, which does not fit.
Conceived means first thought of; the plan already existed and was adjusted.
Displaced means forced out of position, which does not fit.

partsNote: from Latin modus, "measure": to set a measure

definition: the ability to understand and share another person's feelings

examples.text: The novel builds empathy for a character most readers would avoid in life.
Studies suggest that reading fiction improves empathy.
My friend showed real empathy when my dog was sick.

confused.note: Sympathy is feeling sorry for someone; empathy is feeling what they feel.

questions.passage: The best nurses, the director said, combine skill with ______. They not only know how to change a dressing but can also sense when a frightened patient needs a word of reassurance.
questions.explanation: Sensing a patient's fear shows the ability to share another's feelings.

distractors.why: Hedonism is the pursuit of pleasure, which does not fit.
Acquisition is the act of obtaining, which does not fit.
A doctrine is a set of beliefs, which does not fit.

definition: intended to harm or upset other people

examples.text: The cousin spreads a malicious rumor that the will was forged.
The fire was no accident but a malicious act by a dismissed servant.
The malicious software locked every file on the school's computers.

confused.note: Malicious means meant to harm; mischievous means playfully troublesome.

questions.passage: The message was not a harmless joke. It was a ______ attempt to damage a colleague's reputation, sent anonymously to her employer the week before she was due for promotion.
questions.explanation: An anonymous message timed to hurt a colleague is meant to harm.

distractors.why: Decisive means conclusive or quick to decide, which does not fit.
Substantial means large, which is not the contrast with a harmless joke.
Imprudent means unwise; the sentence stresses the intent to harm.

definition: to state firmly that something is true; to insist on a right

examples.text: The colonists asserted their right to be taxed only by their own assembly.
The paper asserts that the two species share a common ancestor.
My sister asserted that the top bunk was hers by law.

confused.note: To assert is to state firmly; to assent is to agree.

questions.passage: The author does not merely suggest that the famous photograph was staged. She ______ it outright, and she devotes a full chapter to the evidence.
questions.explanation: Stating it outright is declaring firmly that it is true.

distractors.why: Depicts means portrays, which does not fit stating a claim.
Absolves means frees from blame, which does not fit.
Modifies means changes slightly, which does not fit.

partsNote: from Latin serere, "to join": to join to oneself, to claim

definition: to happen at the same time; or to be the same or similar

examples.text: The king's visit coincided with the worst flood in fifty years.
The peaks in the two graphs coincide almost exactly.
My birthday coincides with the last day of school this year.

confused.note: To coincide is to happen together or match; to collide is to crash.

questions.passage: The festival was scheduled to ______ with the full moon. Organizers wanted the final concert, held outdoors on the beach, to take place under the brightest possible sky.
questions.explanation: Timing the festival to fall on the full moon is having them happen together.

distractors.why: Constitute means to make up, which does not fit "with the full moon."
Endure means to last or bear, which does not fit.
Emit means to give off, which does not fit.

partsNote: from Latin cadere, "to fall": to fall together upon

definition: being part of the basic nature of something; not coming from outside

examples.text: Radioactive decay is an intrinsic property of the element.
The poem's music is intrinsic to its meaning.
The ring has little intrinsic value, but it was my grandmother's.

confused.note: Intrinsic means coming from within the thing itself; extrinsic means coming from outside.

questions.passage: Some students work only for grades or prizes. Others are driven by ______ interest: they study a subject because they find it fascinating and would do so even if no one were keeping score.
questions.explanation: Interest that comes from the subject itself, not from rewards, is intrinsic.

distractors.why: Illicit means illegal, which does not fit.
Obtrusive means unpleasantly noticeable, which does not fit.
Recurrent means repeated, which is not the contrast with grades and prizes.

definition: giving a lot of information clearly in a few words

examples.text: The abstract should be a concise summary of the whole paper.
The general's concise orders left no room for confusion.
Keep your message concise; nobody reads a text with six paragraphs.

confused.note: Concise means brief and clear; precise means exact.

questions.passage: The guide's entry on the cathedral is admirably ______. In four sentences it gives the building's age, style, and history and tells the visitor which two chapels should not be missed.
questions.explanation: Covering the essentials in four sentences is brief and clear.

distractors.why: Bombastic means inflated and pompous, the opposite of a brief, clear entry.
Dreary means dull and gloomy, which is not what "admirably" introduces.
Divergent means differing, which does not fit.

definition: not allowed by law or by social rules

examples.text: The port was a center of illicit trade in ivory.
The lovers exchange illicit letters through the gardener.
My brother ran an illicit candy business out of his locker.

confused.note: Illicit is an adjective meaning illegal; elicit is a verb meaning to draw out.

questions.passage: Customs officers at the port search every container. Their chief concern is the ______ trade in rare animals, which are smuggled in crates labeled as machine parts.
questions.explanation: Smuggling animals in mislabeled crates is against the law.

distractors.why: Elicit is a verb meaning to draw out; it only sounds like the adjective needed.
Intrinsic means built in, which does not fit.
Egalitarian means favoring equality, which does not fit.

definition: to show someone or something in a picture or describe it in words

examples.text: The novel depicts a town slowly emptied by the closing of its mill.
Cave paintings depict hunters chasing herds of bison.
The mural in our gym depicts every sport the school has ever played.

confused.note: To depict is to portray; to predict is to say what will happen.

questions.passage: Earlier portraits had shown the queen as stern and remote. This painter chose to ______ her differently, seated on the floor with her children and laughing at something outside the frame.
questions.explanation: Showing her in a painting is portraying her.

distractors.why: Incite means to stir up, which does not fit.
Absolve means to free from blame, which does not fit.
Enumerate means to list one by one, which does not fit a portrait.

definition: to form an idea or plan in the mind; to imagine

examples.text: The engineer conceived the canal thirty years before it was dug.
It is hard to conceive of a distance as vast as a light-year.
I cannot conceive of a pizza without cheese.

confused.note: To conceive is to form an idea; to concede is to admit or yield.

questions.passage: The bridge was built in 1932, but it had been ______ much earlier. Sketches found in the engineer's notebooks show that he first imagined the design as a student, nearly forty years before construction began.
questions.explanation: First imagining the design is forming the idea.

distractors.why: Unveiled means revealed publicly, which is not what the sketches show.
Displaced means moved out of position, which does not fit.
Regenerated means grown again, which does not fit.

definition: different from each other; moving apart

examples.text: The two species followed divergent paths after the islands separated.
The allies held divergent views on how to divide the conquered land.
My brother and I have divergent ideas about what counts as a clean room.

confused.note: Divergent means moving or developing apart; diverse means varied.

questions.passage: The two biographers reach sharply ______ conclusions. One presents the general as a brilliant strategist; the other argues that his victories were the work of subordinates whose names he left out of his reports.
questions.explanation: Opposite judgments of the same man are differing conclusions.

distractors.why: Indisputable means beyond doubt, which conflicting conclusions are not.
Recurrent means repeated, which does not fit.
Comparable means similar, the opposite of sharply differing.

partsNote: from Latin vergere, "to bend": bending apart

definition: a person's usual nature and way of feeling and behaving

examples.text: The sisters could not be more unlike in temperament: one fiery, one calm.
The study tracked infants' temperament from birth to age five.
A sheepdog's energetic temperament is wrong for apartment life.

confused.note: Temperament is a person's nature; temperature is a measure of heat.

questions.passage: By ______ the two founders were opposites. One was cautious, quiet, and happiest alone with a spreadsheet; the other was impulsive, talkative, and bored by anything that took longer than an afternoon.
questions.explanation: Being cautious or impulsive by nature is a matter of temperament.

distractors.why: A doctrine is a set of beliefs, which does not fit "by."
Acquisition is obtaining, which does not fit.
Conviction is firm belief; the details describe personality.

definition: to say the opposite of what someone else has said; to be in conflict with

examples.text: The new data contradict the results published last year.
The diary contradicts the general's official account of the battle.
My brother contradicts everything I say on principle.

confused.note: To contradict is to say the opposite or conflict with; to contrast is to show differences.

questions.passage: The witness told the court that she had been at home all evening. Her statement was ______ by a neighbor, who testified that he had seen her car leave at eight and return after midnight.
questions.explanation: The neighbor's testimony conflicts with her statement.

distractors.why: Depicted means portrayed, which does not fit.
Absolved means cleared of blame, which the neighbor's testimony did not do.
Imparted means passed on, which does not fit.

definition: an enemy or opponent

examples.text: The two kingdoms, once allies, became bitter adversaries.
The detective respects his adversary too much to underestimate her.
My chess adversary at lunch is a ten-year-old who has never lost.

confused.note: An adversary is an opponent; adversity is hardship.

questions.passage: The chess champion spoke warmly of her longtime ______. Though they had faced each other in forty tournaments and neither gave an inch at the board, the two often dined together afterward.
questions.explanation: Someone she has faced across the board forty times is her opponent.

distractors.why: Adversity is hardship; it looks similar but is not a person.
A benefactor is a helper or donor, which does not fit someone she plays against.
A predecessor is someone who came before, which does not fit.

definition: to send out gas, heat, light, or sound

examples.text: The firefly emits a cold green light.
The new furnaces emitted so much smoke that the town's stone turned black.
The smoke detector emits a chirp every thirty seconds when its battery is low.

confused.note: To emit is to give off; to omit is to leave out.

questions.passage: Some deep-sea fish ______ their own light. Organs along their sides glow blue in the darkness, attracting prey and helping members of the same species find one another.
questions.explanation: Giving off light is emitting it.

distractors.why: Omit means to leave out; it only resembles the right word.
Secrete means to produce a liquid substance, or to hide; light is given off, not secreted.
Impart means to pass on knowledge or a quality, which does not fit producing light.

definition: happening again and again

examples.text: The patient suffered from recurrent infections each winter.
A recurrent image of locked doors runs through the novel.
I have a recurrent dream about forgetting my locker combination.

confused.note: Recurrent means happening repeatedly; current means happening now.

questions.passage: Flooding is a ______ problem in the lower town. The river has overflowed its banks eleven times in the past twenty years, most recently last spring.
questions.explanation: Eleven floods in twenty years is a problem that keeps returning.

distractors.why: Indisputable means beyond doubt, which is not what the count of floods shows.
Dreary means dull and gloomy, which does not fit.
Illicit means illegal, which does not fit.

definition: to show or announce something publicly for the first time

examples.text: The mayor unveiled a statue of the city's founder.
The company unveiled a battery that charges in five minutes.
My sister unveiled her science fair project to the family after dinner.

confused.note: To unveil is to reveal; to unravel is to come apart or to solve.

questions.passage: The carmaker had kept its new model secret for three years. It finally ______ the vehicle at a ceremony in Geneva, where reporters were allowed to photograph it for the first time.
questions.explanation: Showing the car publicly for the first time is unveiling it.

distractors.why: Secreted can mean hid away, the opposite of showing publicly.
Devised means invented, which happened earlier; the ceremony revealed it.
Displaced means moved out of position, which does not fit.

definition: to plan or invent something using careful thought

examples.text: The engineers devised a pump to keep the mine dry.
The team devised a test that detects the virus in ten minutes.
I devised a system of colored folders to keep my classes straight.

confused.note: Devise is the verb; a device is the thing invented.

questions.passage: Trapped behind enemy lines with no radio, the prisoners ______ an ingenious way to send messages. They hid notes inside hollowed-out buttons, which were sewn onto coats sent home for repair.
questions.explanation: Thinking up a clever method is inventing a plan.

distractors.why: Incited means stirred up, which does not fit.
Enumerated means listed, which does not fit.
Contradicted means conflicted with, which does not fit.

definition: to encourage someone to do something violent or illegal

examples.text: The pamphlet was written to incite the soldiers to mutiny.
The villain incites the crowd against the innocent miller.
My cousin was accused of inciting the great cafeteria food fight.

confused.note: To incite is to stir up; insight is deep understanding.

questions.passage: The court found that the speaker had gone beyond criticism of the government. He had tried to ______ violence, urging his listeners to burn the tax office and promising to lead them there himself.
questions.explanation: Urging listeners to burn a building is encouraging violence.

distractors.why: Absolve means to free from blame, which does not fit.
Depict means to portray, which is far weaker than urging people to act.
Regenerate means to grow again, which does not fit.

definition: to give information, knowledge, or a quality to someone or something

examples.text: Elders imparted the tribe's history to the young through song.
The mineral imparts a blue tint to the glass.
My grandmother imparted her pie crust secret to me alone.

confused.note: To impart is to give or share; to impair is to weaken.

questions.passage: A good teacher does more than ______ facts. She also shows students how to question what they read and how to find answers for themselves.
questions.explanation: Passing facts to students is giving them information.

distractors.why: Incite means to stir up to violence, which does not fit.
Displace means to move out of position, which does not fit.
Secrete means to produce a fluid or to hide, which does not fit teaching.

definition: to force something or someone out of its usual place; to take the place of

examples.text: The dam displaced forty thousand villagers.
A floating object displaces its own weight in water.
The new couch displaced the armchair to the hallway.

confused.note: To displace is to force out of position; to misplace is to lose temporarily.

questions.passage: The construction of the reservoir ______ more than two thousand families. Their villages now lie under thirty meters of water, and most resettled in a new town built on higher ground.
questions.explanation: Families forced to leave their flooded villages were moved from their homes.

distractors.why: Absolved means freed from blame, which does not fit.
Unveiled means revealed, which does not fit.
Imparted means passed on, which does not fit.

definition: true beyond any doubt

examples.text: It is indisputable that the planet's average temperature has risen.
Her indisputable courage at the bridge won the admiration of both armies.
It is indisputable that my grandmother makes the best soup on the street.

confused.note: Indisputable means beyond doubt; indispensable means absolutely necessary.

questions.passage: Whether the policy was wise is open to debate. That it was expensive is ______: official figures show that it cost three times the original estimate.
questions.explanation: Official figures put the cost beyond doubt.

distractors.why: Divergent means differing, which does not fit.
Imprudent means unwise, which is the part the passage says is debatable.
Egalitarian means favoring equality, which does not fit.

partsNote: from Latin putare, "to think": not able to be argued apart

definition: to declare that someone is free from blame, guilt, or responsibility

examples.text: The inquiry absolved the captain of any fault in the sinking.
The priest absolves the dying soldier.
Finding the vase already cracked absolved me of breaking it.

confused.note: To absolve is to free from blame; to dissolve is to melt into a liquid or to end.

questions.passage: The report did not ______ the engineers entirely. It found that although the storm was unusually severe, they should have known that the drainage system could not handle even an ordinary flood.
questions.explanation: The report did not free them from all blame.

distractors.why: Incite means to stir up, which does not fit.
Enumerate means to list, which does not fit.
Depict means to portray, which does not capture clearing someone of blame.

definition: to produce and release a liquid; or to hide something

examples.text: Glands in the skin secrete oil that keeps hair from drying out.
The spy secreted the map in the lining of his coat.
The dog had secreted three socks behind the couch.

confused.note: To secrete is to produce a fluid or to hide; a secret is something kept hidden.

questions.passage: When threatened, the toad's skin ______ a bitter, milky fluid. Predators that take the animal into their mouths usually drop it at once and learn to avoid others of its kind.
questions.explanation: Skin producing and releasing a fluid is secreting it.

distractors.why: Emits means gives off light, gas, heat, or sound; a liquid produced by glands is secreted.
Imparts means passes on knowledge or a quality, which does not fit.
Unveils means reveals publicly, which does not fit.

definition: using long, important-sounding words that have little meaning

examples.text: The dictator's bombastic speeches lasted for hours and said nothing.
The mayor's bombastic toast compares the new fountain to the pyramids.
The ad's bombastic claims about "revolutionizing breakfast" were about a toaster.

confused.note: Bombastic means pompously wordy; to bombard is to attack continuously.

questions.passage: The prospectus was full of ______ language. It promised investors "a paradigm of unparalleled magnificence" and "horizons of limitless grandeur," but nowhere did it say what the company actually made.
questions.explanation: Grand phrases with no content are inflated, empty language.

distractors.why: Concise means brief and clear, the opposite of this language.
Treacherous means disloyal or dangerous, which does not describe wordiness.
Dreary means dull and gloomy, which does not fit showy phrases.

partsNote: from an old word for cotton padding

definition: to name things one by one in a list

examples.text: The petition enumerated twenty-seven grievances against the king.
The report enumerates the species found at each site.
My mother enumerated the chores I had not done.

confused.note: To enumerate is to list; to enunciate is to pronounce clearly.

questions.passage: The contract does not speak of the tenant's duties in general terms. It ______ them, setting out in forty numbered clauses everything from the watering of the garden to the hours at which music may be played.
questions.explanation: Setting out duties in numbered clauses is listing them one by one.

distractors.why: Contradicts means conflicts with, which does not fit.
Displaces means moves out of position, which does not fit.
Conceives means forms an idea, which does not fit listing duties.

partsNote: from Latin numerus, "number": to count out

definition: not wise or sensible; showing poor judgment

examples.text: The king's imprudent loans to his friends emptied the treasury.
It was imprudent of the heroine to trust a stranger with the letter.
It was imprudent to wear new shoes on a ten-mile hike.

confused.note: Imprudent means unwise; impudent means rude and disrespectful.

questions.passage: Financial advisers considered the purchase ______. The couple had spent their entire savings on a house they had seen only in photographs, in a town where neither had ever found work.
questions.explanation: Spending all their savings on an unseen house shows poor judgment.

distractors.why: Indisputable means beyond doubt, which does not describe a risky purchase.
Egalitarian means favoring equality, which does not fit.
Impudent means disrespectful; it looks like the right word but does not mean unwise.

definition: not able to be trusted; or dangerous, especially when seeming safe

examples.text: The treacherous governor opened the city gates to the enemy at night.
The glacier is treacherous, its crevasses hidden under fresh snow.
The icy steps were treacherous this morning.

confused.note: Treacherous can mean disloyal or dangerous; traitorous means only betraying one's country or cause.

questions.passage: Sailors regard the strait as ______. Its surface often looks calm, but powerful currents beneath can drag a small boat onto the rocks within minutes.
questions.explanation: Water that looks calm but hides deadly currents is dangerous while seeming safe.

distractors.why: Dreary means dull and gloomy, which does not convey hidden danger.
Scandalous means shocking and disgraceful, which does not describe a strait.
Recurrent means repeated, which does not fit.

definition: shocking because it is morally wrong or disgraceful

examples.text: The minister's scandalous use of public money ended his career.
The village finds it scandalous that the widow dances at the fair.
The price of popcorn at the cinema is scandalous.

confused.note: Scandalous describes the shocking thing; scandalized describes the person who is shocked.

questions.passage: Newspapers called the affair ______. The official in charge of the city's water supply, it emerged, had for years sold clean water to private firms while poor neighborhoods went without.
questions.explanation: Profiting while poor neighborhoods went without water is shockingly wrong.

distractors.why: Egalitarian means treating people equally, the opposite of what the official did.
Imprudent means merely unwise, far too mild for deliberate wrongdoing.
Bombastic means pompously wordy, which does not fit.

definition: to grow again or bring new life to something

examples.text: A starfish can regenerate a lost arm within months.
The new port regenerated a town that had been declining for a century.
A weekend of sleep regenerated my will to study.

confused.note: To regenerate is to grow again or renew; to degenerate is to decline.

questions.passage: Unlike most organs, the liver has a remarkable capacity to ______. A patient who donates half of the organ can expect it to return to nearly its full size within three months.
questions.explanation: An organ returning to full size is growing again.

distractors.why: Secrete means to produce a fluid, which is not the capacity described.
Displace means to move out of position, which does not fit.
Emit means to give off, which does not fit.

definition: dull, gloomy, and making you feel sad or bored

examples.text: The novel opens on a dreary stretch of marsh under a gray sky.
Soldiers wrote home about the dreary routine of camp life.
Sunday was dreary: rain, homework, and nothing good in the fridge.

confused.note: Dreary means dull and gloomy; weary means tired.

questions.passage: The town in winter is a ______ place. Shops close at four, the single café serves only tea, and for weeks at a time the fog is so thick that the harbor cannot be seen from the main street.
questions.explanation: Early closings and weeks of fog make a dull, gloomy place.

distractors.why: Scandalous means shockingly wrong, which does not fit.
Treacherous means dangerous or disloyal; the details stress dullness and gloom.
Bombastic means pompously wordy, which does not fit.

definition: believing that all people are equal and should have the same rights and opportunities

examples.text: The reformers imagined an egalitarian society with no titles or ranks.
Wolf packs are less egalitarian than was once believed.
Our team is egalitarian about snacks: everyone brings, everyone shares.

confused.note: Egalitarian means favoring equality; utilitarian means practical.

questions.passage: The cooperative is run on ______ principles. Every member, from the newest baker to the founder, earns the same wage, has one vote at meetings, and takes a turn at washing the floors.
questions.explanation: Equal wages, votes, and chores reflect a belief in equality.

distractors.why: Illicit means illegal, which does not fit.
Bombastic means pompously wordy, which does not fit.
Imprudent means unwise, which is not what the details show.
